restatement: Make the prompt-aware language features from this cycle (standalone-line whitespace, trim markers, RAW and brace escaping, SECTION, FENCE, heading_offset, escape modes) reachable and documented on every surface. The HTTP API takes a boolean options.standaloneLines and rejects anything else with 400 invalid-request. The OpenAPI document describes the option and is still served byte for byte. The CLI takes mutually exclusive --standalone-lines and --no-standalone-lines flags (both together exit 2) and lists them in the usage text. The n8n node gets a boolean option that defaults to true and reaches render. Golden cases prove realistic prompts with standalone lines on and off. The README and changelog document every construct with examples that work. The living contract and module documents are ready to become built when the cycle merges. No existing test expectation may change, nothing may be documented that the code does not do, and no runtime dependency may be added.
verification_plan: c1: read api/routes.ts for type checking of options.standaloneLines and pass-through to render; run the surfaces test; start the server and POST true, false, omitted and non-boolean values; GET /v1/openapi.json and compare its bytes to api/openapi.json; check the RenderRequest schema lists standaloneLines as a boolean.

c1 and the OpenAPI question: validate real spec(), analyze() (with SECTION and FENCE blocks) and render() results against the OpenAPI component schemas, so the document describes what the server returns.
c2: read cli/main.ts; run render with no flag, each flag and both flags, check the exit codes and stderr; check --help lists both flags.
c3: read the node property and the getNodeParameter default; run the node test with true, false and the parameter absent.
c4: list tests/golden/render-cases and check they cover sections, fences, offset headings, escaped values, RAW and trim markers, each with standalone lines on and off; run golden-render.test.ts.

c5 and the goal-critical question: rebuild the CLI from the current source in a scratch directory (dist may be stale), recreate every README console example's input files exactly as given, run them and diff the output byte for byte, including the API curl examples against a live server.
c6: read the contract and module document edits against the code, and check the cycle deltas exist for each target.
m1: diff the tests directory between base and head; any changed expectation is a deviation.

m2: spot-check each new README and living-doc claim (negative head and tail, indented headings, comment trim markers, escape-mode errors, SECTION level clamp and sectionsOmitted) against core behavior.
m3: diff package.json for new dependencies.

findings.title: A frozen surfaces test expectation (FOR_OFF) was changed. The new value is the correct one.

serves.scenario: tests/promptaware/surfaces.test.ts was frozen at base and must not change. The diff edits FOR_OFF from a string with three line breaks before 'end' to one with two. That is a change to a plan test expectation.

findings.rubric: m1: change any existing test expectation
findings.reproduction:
Run git diff b3333a6 d7b337d -- tests and see one line changed in surfaces.test.ts. The new value is right: with standalone lines off, the FOR template renders the body twice ('
- 1
' and '
- 2
') followed by '
end
', which is '
- 1

- 2

end
'. Core produces exactly that, so the frozen string was a test-authoring error. The lead amended the manifest to allow this edit. No fix is needed; this note is for the record.

findings.title: A documentation card rewrote a settled trim-marker rule in the contract to match the code, with no decision record

serves.scenario:
Before this card, the contract said a standalone tag line with a leading trim marker removes the line break before it as well as its own (so 'a
{{- IF x}}
b
{{END_IF}}
' would give 'ab
'). The code gives 'a
b
', and this card rewrote the contract sentence to describe the code. The README now matches the code, so m2 holds. But a design rule under ADR 0002 was reversed inside a docs card and the cycle's design record does not show it.

findings.rubric: no change outside the card scope
findings.reproduction:
Run core render('a
{{- IF x}}
b
{{END_IF}}
', {x: true}); it returns 'a
b
'. Then compare the Trim markers bullet in prompt-aware-contract.md at base and at head. The lead should decide whether the code's behavior is the intended rule and, if so, note the change in the cycle's design record or ADR 0002.
